evidence: Verg. A. 4.493: magicās … artēs (Lewis & Short, s.v. magicus)
terms.comment: Usually plural, artēs magicae; magicus is poetic and post-Augustan (Lewis & Short). A magician is magus, a witch maga or saga.

evidence: Cic. Brut. 217: venēficiīs et cantiōnibus Titiniae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Its first sense is poisoning; then the brewing of magic potions and spells. Black magic rather than a conjuror’s tricks (see magic trick).
Greek; Apuleius’s word in his defence against a charge of magic, and Prudentius’s.

evidence: Cato Agr. 160: hāc cantiōne sānum fīet
terms.comment: A song, and so a sung charm; also carmen (carmina magica).

terms.register: vōx poētica et post-Augustēa (Lewis & Short: poet. and post-Aug. prose)

phrases.english: these, citizens, are my magic spells

phrases.latin: luxum sīquod est, hāc cantiōne sānum fīet
phrases.english: if anything is out of joint, it will be healed with this spell
